faq.a: Mostly to communicate and to control temperature. Males flash bright colours at rivals and mates, frightened ones may go dark, and a cold chameleon darkens to soak up more sunlight. Matching the background is a smaller part.
asks: Do chameleons change colour to hide?
Why do chameleons go dark when cold?

faq.a: Iridophores are skin cells packed with tiny guanine crystals arranged in a regular lattice. The spacing of the crystals decides which colours of light bounce back, like the shimmer on a soap bubble.

faq.q: How do the crystals make different colours?
faq.a: Light reflects from many crystal layers. When the layers are close, short blue waves add up and bounce back; when the chameleon spreads them, longer yellow and red waves are reflected instead.
asks: How does crystal spacing change colour?

faq.q: Why is a calm chameleon green?
faq.a: A relaxed chameleon's crystals reflect blue light. That blue passes through a layer of yellow pigment above, and blue plus yellow looks green.

faq.q: How fast can a chameleon change colour?
faq.a: A panther chameleon can shift colour in a minute or two, and some quick flushes take seconds. Octopuses and squid, which use muscles, can change much faster.

facts: In 2015 scientists showed that panther chameleons change colour by changing the spacing of guanine nanocrystals in skin cells called iridophores.
Chameleons change colour mainly for signalling and temperature control rather than camouflage.

quiz.say: When a panther chameleon gets excited, what happens to the crystals in its skin?
quiz.why: Wider spacing makes the lattice reflect longer wavelengths, shifting the colour towards yellow and red.

wrong.1: The crystals stay solid; only their spacing changes.
wrong.2: Crystals reflect light by their structure; they do not become pigment.

quiz.say: What is the main reason chameleons change colour?

options.show: Signal to others and control temperature
options.say: Signal to others and control temperature

quiz.why: Colour displays settle fights and attract mates, and darker skin warms the body.

wrong.1: Background matching is a minor role, despite the popular idea.
wrong.2: Insects are their food; colour change is not aimed at them.
